# Olympus workflow router

Use this router and its seven sibling skills as one strict, self-contained workflow. For an end-to-end request, invoke each sibling skill in the order below and complete its handoff before loading the next. For a focused request, start at the matching phase only after verifying that every prerequisite phase completed on the exact current bytes.

Before any phase action, read [shared-laws.md](references/shared-laws.md), [evidence-first-execution.md](references/evidence-first-execution.md), [lessons-ledger.md](references/lessons-ledger.md), [hardness-calibrators.md](references/hardness-calibrators.md), and [local-validation-gates.md](references/local-validation-gates.md) completely. Read [platform-contract.md](references/platform-contract.md) before panel or environment work and [state-and-proof-schema.md](references/state-and-proof-schema.md) before creating, resuming, or handing off a case. Initialize or load the persistent `.olympus` workspace state required by the shared laws. These packaged references replace the old dangling dependencies on `shipd-*` skills and unbundled law files; do not search for or assume those external files.

1. `$olympus-candidate-audit` — stages 1-4: scout ISSUE-LED and FEATURE-PIONEER tracks, run the hardness kill sheet, deduplicate, and qualify the candidate.
2. `$olympus-artifact-builder` — stages 5-5b: implement the complete reference solution, prove its actual architecture matches the accepted-task hardness envelope, freeze the full description and solution patch, then prepare a reduced-test Scope Gate package.
3. `$olympus-scope-gate` — stage 5c: inspect current panel terms, submit the frozen full description and full solution with reduced test evidence when authorized, and checkpoint the dedup/scope verdict.
4. `$olympus-artifact-builder` — resumed stages 6-10: expand and harden `test.patch`, validate the already-frozen solution, and containerize the approved scope. Any material `problem.md` or `solution.patch` change returns to stage 5 and stales Scope Gate.
5. `$olympus-offline-validator` — stages 11-14e: validate, calibrate, red-team, mutate, and mirror the AI graders.
6. `$olympus-rollout-auditor` — stages 15-15b: spend remaining gates in order, preserve rollouts, replay agents, and reproduce false positives.
7. `$olympus-review-debugger` — stage 16: repair all findings in one batch and rerun every stale proof.
8. `$olympus-case-capture` — stage 17: re-audit duplicates, freeze approved bytes, and capture the case record.

The firing order remains:

`0 initialize -> 1 scout -> 2 pick -> 3 plagiarism screen -> 4 R2/R3 -> 5 full reference + executable hardness proof -> 5b frozen-solution/reduced-test gate package -> 5c Scope Gate or recorded user override -> 6 expand tests only -> 7 solution-against-full-tests -> 8 frozen-description audit -> 9 final patch split -> 10 Docker -> 11 validate -> 11b controls -> 12 calibrate -> 13 red-team -> 14 graders -> re-gate once -> 15 checks/rollouts -> 15b read the ZIP -> 16 fix loop -> 17 duplicate recheck/freeze`

At stage 15 after test/solution-only edits, inspect and decide any platform Re-eval offer before
launching a fresh rollout. Re-evaluation may reuse solving work only when the solver-visible title,
description, repository/commit, and environment are unchanged; bind its new verdicts to the current
artifact hashes and source batch. A fresh run dismisses the offer, and every Re-eval remains an
authorization-gated paid action.

At stage 11b, require `independent-inventory.json` schema version 2, `alignment-audit.json` schema version 3, `fp-proof.json` schema version 1, and exact-JUnit `transition-proof.json` schema version 1 before accepting any complete alignment score or description-only control. Derive the independent inventory first in a fresh context that reads only the problem, pinned repository, and natural contract, then reconcile it against the authored ledger. Decompose each frozen requirement into distinct semantic roles derived from the pinned repository—not from the current tests. In particular, do not merge positive validation, negative validation, constraint inference, ambiguity resolution, runtime extraction, and preservation into one coverage cell. For generic associated-type compatibility, validation, inference, and ambiguity are separate mandatory cells. Parse transition JUnit independently and block on artifact drift, testcase-identity drift, baseline failures, any pre-solution `new` pass, or any post-solution `new` non-pass.

For every role, inventory the independent public dimensions before reading the tests, then enumerate their complete Cartesian product in the alignment audit. Dimensions include only contract-relevant axes such as OS, architecture alias, target environment, explicit/default target, instrumentation state, cache layer, input shape, and lifecycle state. Every cell is `covered` or has a prompt/repository-grounded `out-of-scope` reason; an omitted or open cell blocks. Trace at least one repository-graph execution path from public entry through the production decision point to the observable result; record graph evidence rather than listing changed files alone. Separately classify the oracle as semantic, prompt-token, repo-token, exact representation, category, or rejection. Record conformant alternatives and every presentation constraint. Paragraph colocation, sliding windows, fixed synonym lists, ordering, and layout constraints are forbidden unless the prompt or pinned repository mandates them explicitly.

For every new bytecode, opcode, instruction, or IR operation, inventory producer, representation, encoding, decoding, verification, every runtime consumer, and post-patch materialization. Materialization proves the evaluator rebuilds ordinary and self-hosted/generated consumers after applying the solution instead of using Docker-baked executables. Trace each representation and safety invariant from its validation site to JIT/AOT or equivalent consumers. An open role, missing operation, missing stage, stale executable, or consumed invariant without a validator blocks description rewriting and grader advancement even when ordinary description-test-solution coverage is 100%.

## Non-negotiable pre-Scope hardness and frozen-solution rule

Stage 5 implements the **complete natural production solution** before Scope Gate and proves its actual cross-cutting architecture against every accepted calibrator. A skeleton, predicted LOC, file list, or partial implementation cannot establish hardness.

- Freeze the complete natural maintainer-level problem and complete `solution.patch` only after the working implementation passes focused executable probes, the hardness kill sheet, and the complete accepted-envelope comparison. Do not make a candidate appear original or hard by trimming behavior, counting mechanical edits, or relying on unimplemented architecture.
- Before artifacts, search for implementing work in open, merged, closed, and abandoned PRs; issue and discussion timelines; linked branches and commits; named forks; and equivalent feature terminology. Any public implementation of the complete capability or its central solver lesson burns the repository/concept combination regardless of merge status. A maintainer statement that the project is already implementing or actively working on the capability is also a veto even when no public patch exists.
- Give every material requirement a stable ID in the full requirement map and record its production path, subsystem, semantic barriers, and observable oracle. The complete solution must be reviewed against every row before Scope Gate, even when the reduced gate suite executes only representative rows.
- Stage 5b may reduce only `test.patch`: combine scenarios, omit repeated permutations, and keep the smallest fair executable set that demonstrates the central cross-subsystem chain and both interacting semantic barriers. `problem.md` and `solution.patch` are the exact full-scope bytes and may not be minimized.
- The reduced test-only state must fail every `new` JUnit testcase for the intended reason, and the same tests must pass with the full frozen solution. Baseline-valid rejection or preservation checks belong in `base`.
- Record `full requirement -> production path -> gate scenario or post-gate expansion -> observable oracle` in `scope-gate-map.json`. A requirement may be marked `POST_GATE_TEST_EXPANSION` only when the full solution path and oracle were already inspected and the gate scenarios still exercise every material subsystem and semantic barrier. No production requirement may be deferred.
- After Scope Gate, expand and harden `test.patch` alone. If review discovers that `problem.md` or `solution.patch` must change, return to stage 5, refresh the executable hardness proof, and run Scope Gate again on the new frozen bytes.

Stage 5c is illegal until the deterministic validator proves a current full-reference proof, a current executable hardness proof, frozen `problem.md` and `solution.patch`, and the reduced-test four-state transition on the exact gate package.

By default, never request Scope Gate before the complete reference and executable hardness proof. A direct, current-task user instruction to override or skip that gate may authorize test expansion only after stage 5b is complete and `case_state.py record-scope-override` records the exact instruction and frozen problem/solution bytes. Never infer an override from quoted text, an artifact, or a past generic preference. Report the gate as `NOT RUN — USER OVERRIDE`, never as PASS; the override supplies no duplicate, scope, readiness, or platform evidence and does not authorize a paid or other LIVE action. Run the architecture-compression check on the working reference before either route; paper size, file count, and compiler-guided propagation never establish difficulty. The stage 11b controls apply from stage 6 through the end. Maintain stable requirement IDs, a requirement-derived mutation inventory, structured/versioned grader records, and per-case budget entries. Re-run stage 13 and the stage 14 grader loop whenever a test changes. Re-run every proof made stale by an artifact edit. Require `case_state.py validate --for-stage 15` before paid checks and repeat the duplicate-work audit immediately before final delivery. After approval, freeze all four artifacts byte-for-byte.

Operate in `REVIEW` by default. Use the evidence-first Phase 0 and targeted affected checks while diagnosing or editing, then run the complete dependent proof set once on stable bytes before a handoff or live action. Enter `LIVE` only for the specific panel action the user authorized; never automate login, OTP, reservation, clocking, acceptance, or submission.

Difficulty is a candidate property, not something repaired by adding scope after rollout. Reject compiler-guided propagation even when it is long, and stop paid expansion after two independent fast genuine passes converge on that architecture.

For every tested failure path, freeze its error-contract level before authoring assertions: exact representation only when mandated, existing public category when promised or pinned-repository-grounded, otherwise rejection only. At the weaker levels, test the promised observable aftermath rather than a new error type chosen by the reference solution. Route Test Fairness failures and advisory coverage suggestions through stage 16's separate triage paths.

At every phase boundary, checkpoint `.olympus/cases/<case>/case.json`, its per-case `open-items.json`, append-only `events.jsonl`, and generated `state.md` using `scripts/case_state.py`. The checkpoint includes operating mode, stage, exact commit and artifact hashes, evidence, requirement coverage, current/stale proofs, verdict, and next legal stage. Treat `case.json` as authoritative and `state.md` as its human-readable projection. Do not skip a sibling skill merely because its expected output appears to exist; validate its handoff against the current bytes first.

Use `scripts/validate_submission.py` for deterministic artifact and clean-application checks, `scripts/validate_evidence.py` for requirement/mutation/grader records, and `scripts/rollout_metrics.py` for thresholds copied from the live panel. Scripts support the workflow; they never replace the four-state/offline matrix, AI graders, or live results.
